quests.question: My little sister loves cats ___ dogs equally.
quests.hint: She feels the same way about both animals.
quests.explanation: 'And' links two ideas that are both true — she loves both animals equally.

quests.question: The soup smelled wonderful, ___ it tasted quite bland.
quests.hint: The taste didn't match the amazing smell.
quests.explanation: 'But' joins two contrasting ideas: a great smell led to a disappointing taste.

quests.question: Please turn off the lights ___ you leave the room.
quests.hint: The lights should go off at one exact moment.
quests.explanation: 'When' points to the exact time something happens — turning off the lights matches the moment of leaving.

quests.question: It started to snow, ___ the children ran outside to play.
quests.hint: The snow directly caused their excited reaction.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — the snow is the cause, and running outside is the effect.

quests.question: Grandma is resting ___ she has a headache.
quests.hint: Her headache explains why she needs to rest.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for an action — the headache is why she is resting.

quests.question: Always wash the vegetables ___ you cook them.
quests.hint: One action must happen first, ahead of the other.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows the order of two actions — washing comes earlier than cooking.

quests.question: For dessert, would you prefer cake ___ ice cream?
quests.hint: Only one dessert will be chosen, not both.
quests.explanation: 'Or' offers a choice between two options — the listener picks just one.

quests.question: You can join the team ___ you attend practice every week.
quests.hint: Attending practice is the condition for joining.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces a condition — joining the team depends on this one requirement.

quests.question: Dad reads the newspaper ___ Mom makes breakfast.
quests.hint: Two people are busy with different tasks at the same moment.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows two actions happening at the same time — reading and cooking happen together.

quests.question: We went home ___ the movie finished.
quests.hint: One event ended, and then the other one started.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows one event follows another — going home came once the movie was over.

quests.question: Keep stirring the sauce ___ it thickens.
quests.hint: The stirring continues all the way up to one point.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the stopping point of a continuous action — stirring shouldn't stop before the sauce thickens.

quests.question: She packed her bag ___ locked the front door.
quests.hint: Two simple actions happened one after another, both completed.
quests.explanation: 'And' joins two actions the same person did in sequence — packing and locking both happened.

quests.question: We won't have the picnic ___ the weather improves.
quests.hint: Think 'if not' — better weather is the one thing that would change this.
quests.explanation: 'Unless' means 'except if' — the picnic depends entirely on this one condition.

quests.question: ___ the backpack was heavy, she carried it all the way up the hill.
quests.hint: A real difficulty is acknowledged, but it didn't stop her.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a fact that makes the rest surprising — despite the heavy bag, she still made the climb.

quests.question: The kids were exhausted, ___ they fell asleep during the car ride.
quests.hint: Their tiredness directly led to falling asleep.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — being exhausted caused them to fall asleep.

quests.question: I always feel nervous ___ I speak in front of the class.
quests.hint: The nervous feeling happens at one specific moment.
quests.explanation: 'When' marks the exact situation that triggers a feeling — speaking in class causes the nerves.

quests.question: He studied all night, ___ he still failed the quiz.
quests.hint: Hard work didn't lead to the result you'd expect.
quests.explanation: 'But' shows an unexpected contrast — effort here didn't lead to success.

quests.question: The picnic was cancelled ___ it started to rain.
quests.hint: Rain is the direct reason for the cancellation.
quests.explanation: 'Because' explains the cause of an event — rain is why the picnic was cancelled.

quests.question: Try not to talk ___ the teacher is explaining the lesson.
quests.hint: Both things would be happening at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two actions happening at once — the request is to avoid talking during the explanation.

quests.question: Should we walk ___ take the bus to school?
quests.hint: Two travel methods are offered, and only one will be chosen.
quests.explanation: 'Or' presents a choice between two options in a question.

quests.question: Brush your teeth ___ you go to bed.
quests.hint: One habit should always be the very first step in the bedtime routine.
quests.explanation: 'Before' places one action ahead of another in time — brushing comes first, sleeping comes after.

quests.question: You will get wet ___ you forget your umbrella.
quests.hint: Getting wet depends on one missing item.
quests.explanation: 'If' sets a condition — forgetting the umbrella is what would cause getting wet.

quests.question: The cat stretched, yawned, ___ curled up on the sofa.
quests.hint: This is the final item in a simple list of actions.
quests.explanation: 'And' connects the last item in a list of actions — it simply completes the sequence.

quests.question: The baby cried ___ her mother picked her up.
quests.hint: The crying stopped at one specific moment.
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows the ending point of a continuous action — the crying continued up to that moment.

quests.question: We boarded the train ___ our platform number was announced.
quests.hint: Boarding happened at one exact announced moment.
quests.explanation: 'When' introduces the exact time boarding took place — right after the announcement.

quests.question: We missed our flight ___ traffic was terrible.
quests.hint: Traffic explains why the flight was missed.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for missing the flight — heavy traffic was the cause.

quests.question: The hotel room was small, ___ the view was beautiful.
quests.hint: One disappointing detail is balanced by a surprising positive one.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — a small room is offset by a beautiful view.

quests.question: She stayed home from work ___ she caught a cold.
quests.hint: Illness explains her absence from work.
quests.explanation: 'Because' explains the reason for staying home — a cold is the cause.

quests.question: He felt dizzy, ___ he sat down immediately.
quests.hint: Feeling dizzy led directly to an action.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces the result of feeling dizzy — sitting down was the response.

quests.question: ___ she felt tired, she finished the whole race.
quests.hint: Tiredness is real, but it didn't stop her from finishing.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces a concession — despite being tired, she still completed the race.
